newsitem.title: USA: Washington state Gov. vetoes property tax bill.
newsitem.headline: Washington state Gov. vetoes property tax bill.

text.p: Washington Gov. Gary Locke on Wednesday vetoed legislation that would have permanently reduced state property taxes.

In its place, Locke submitted legislation for a one-year extension of the temporary property tax reduction and said he would continue to work on a comprehensive tax relief package to benefit homeowners and businesses in the state.
Locke vetoed House Bill 1037, which would have made a 4.7 percent state property tax levy reduction permanent.
In his veto message, Locke said the bill did not provide enough relief to homeowners.

"I'm prepared to work with legislative leaders to develop the best tax-relief package possible," Locke said in a statement. "We need to judge every public policy by whether it helps or hurts Washington's working families."
Locke sent the Legislature his own proposal to continue last year's 4.7 percent reduction in state property tax rates for one year.
Locke said he was also prepared to roll back business and occupation taxes to pre-1993 levels.
More than a dozen property tax measures have been introduced since the state Legislature convened last week.
Locke said he favors an approach that would provide a tax credit to individual homeowners for a certain portion of their home's assessed value.
